column1: Updated read incorporating SLOOS: The FOMC’s March 2018 statement points to a strengthening economy and low unemployment, with inflation moving toward 2% and policy tightening proceeding gradually. The January 2018 SLOOS adds that banks broadly eased C&I standards and narrowed loan rate spreads, especially for middle‑market firms, citing competition and an improved economic outlook, and some expect to ease standards for small firms—supportive for growth. Offsetting this, banks tightened standards for CRE and construction/land development, reported weaker demand in those segments, tightened certain other terms, and expect to tighten CRE standards further. On the consumer side, standards were largely unchanged, but banks anticipate some deterioration in credit card and HELOC performance. Taken together with elevated asset valuations and rising corporate leverage, the credit backdrop looks accommodative but more mixed, tempering the otherwise positive macro tone. sentiment score = 0.36
